title: Harden v2 cancellation races and lifecycle events
objective: Correct additive llm/request/v2 cancellation race behavior and make cancellation lifecycle transitions observable without redesigning the WI-0005 DebugSink and AbortSignal boundaries.

branch.name: wi-0007-v2-cancellation-hardening
branch.rationale: The work item is processed as a serial set of scoped commits on the current repository branch; the branch name records the follow-up correctness boundary without requiring a topic branch.

request.text: Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* in the llm repository to harden v2 cancellation races and lifecycle events: cancel after llm.provider.response before terminal success, prevent later parallel tools after cancellation during llm.tool.call, emit explicit llm.cancel.observed and llm.cancelled events, and use a dedicated cancellation error phase. Keep the scope additive to v2 and preserve WI-0006 and unrelated changes. Commit the documentation.

scope.name: v2-cancellation-race-hardening
scope.description: Ensure cancellation observed after provider responses or during tool-call event emission prevents later terminal/model/tool work while preserving settled results.
scope.reason: WI-0005 established cancellation plumbing but current control points allow monitor-triggered races to fall through to success or start later parallel calls.

scope.name: v2-cancellation-lifecycle-contract
scope.description: Add explicit bounded llm.cancel.observed and llm.cancelled DebugSink events and represent CANCELLED diagnostics with a dedicated cancellation phase.
scope.reason: Monitors need to distinguish cancellation observation and completion from ordinary provider, retry, or tool events.

nonGoals.name: v1-contract-mutation
nonGoals.description: Do not change llm/request/v1, llm/response/v1, or their behavior.
nonGoals.reason: The follow-up is additive to v2 and must preserve existing v1 compatibility.

nonGoals.name: observer-redesign
nonGoals.description: Do not add a second observer API, callback field, stream abstraction, or request-embedded monitor object.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0005 already selected DebugSink as the event transport; this work only completes its cancellation lifecycle semantics.

nonGoals.name: runtime-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not add LangGraph, persistence, checkpointing, resume, interrupt/resume, provider expansion, rollback, or forced termination of arbitrary tools.
nonGoals.reason: The fix is local to the existing v2 completion loop, provider boundary, error contract, and deterministic tests.

nonGoals.name: unrelated-work-items
nonGoals.description: Do not modify WI-0006 executable sample records or absorb unrelated request-schema changes.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0006 is a separate planned work item and existing request-schema changes are outside this follow-up.

nonGoals.name: operational-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not claim authenticated provider behavior, real external tool effects, production readiness, or downstream integration.
nonGoals.reason: Evidence remains provider-free, deterministic, and cooperative.

items.name: post-provider-response-cancellation
items.description: Cancellation observed after llm.provider.response is emitted is handled before terminal output processing and returns cancelled rather than success.
items.reason: A monitor can abort from the provider-response event and must not allow the already-returned response to bypass cancellation policy.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A deterministic test aborts from the llm.provider.response DebugSink event and asserts status cancelled, a CANCELLED diagnostic, no terminal success, and the expected final event sequence.

items.name: parallel-tool-cancellation-boundary
items.description: Cancellation observed during llm.tool.call prevents later unstarted calls in the same parallel batch from invoking while allowing already-started calls to settle cooperatively.
items.reason: Promise.all batch mapping currently creates all invocation callbacks synchronously, so event-triggered cancellation needs an explicit pre-invocation boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A deterministic parallel-batch test aborts from the first llm.tool.call event and proves later unstarted tools are not invoked, the result is cancelled, and settled results are preserved or classified consistently.

items.name: explicit-cancellation-events
items.description: The runtime emits bounded llm.cancel.observed and llm.cancelled events through DebugSink with stable ordering and phase/counter metadata.
items.reason: Monitors need to distinguish cancellation observation from final cancellation completion without inferring either from a terminal response alone.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tests verify provider-phase and tool-phase cancellation event sequences, bounded sanitized metadata, and one final llm.cancelled event before llm.response.

items.name: cancellation-phase-and-regression-contract
items.description: CANCELLED diagnostics use a dedicated cancellation error phase and all existing v1/v2, event, cancellation, schema, build, and scope checks remain green.
items.reason: Cancellation is neither provider retry nor ordinary tool invocation failure and should be routable as its own bounded condition.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The TypeScript error phase, response/v2 schema, response construction, documentation, and deterministic tests agree on cancellation; package gates pass; WI-0006 and unrelated request-schema paths remain untouched.
